title: Finding revenue figures in a quarterly report
description: A user asks for Q3 revenue from a 60-page PDF. RLM inspects the document programmatically instead of trying to fit it into one prompt.

steps.title: Question received
steps.summary: The user asks about a document that is too large or complex for a simple one-pass answer.

details.prompt: What was Q3 revenue, and how did it compare to Q2?

steps.title: Plan formed
steps.summary: The model decides to inspect the document iteratively rather than load it into the prompt. It plans to chunk the PDF text and search for revenue mentions.

details.prompt: Document is 60 pages (≈ 38000 tokens). Approach: load into REPL as `prompt`, search for 'revenue' across all chunks, then read 200-token windows around the strongest hits.

steps.title: Code generated
steps.summary: The model writes a small Python action that searches the document for revenue mentions and returns the surrounding context.

details.code:
hits = grep(prompt, pattern="revenue")
windows = [peek(prompt, start=h - 200, length=400) for h in hits[:6]]
print(len(hits), "matches")
print(windows)

steps.title: Sandbox executed
steps.summary: The REPL runs the code and returns an observation. Twelve revenue mentions, six high-signal windows surfaced.

details.output:
12 matches
["... Q3 revenue of $4.2B, up from $3.8B in Q2 ...", "... revenue growth driven by ...", "... segment revenue mix ...", "... revenue guidance for Q4 ...", "... deferred revenue rose to ...", "... revenue per user climbed to ..."]

steps.title: Decision point
steps.summary: The first window already contains both Q3 and Q2 revenue figures. The model decides it has enough information and stops recursing.

details.prompt: Window 1 contains the answer (Q3 $4.2B, Q2 $3.8B). No need to chunk further or call sub_RLM.

steps.title: Final answer
steps.summary: The system returns the answer along with the cost and latency totals for the run.

details.output: Q3 revenue was $4.2B, up from $3.8B in Q2 — a sequential increase of about 10.5%.
